mainTopic: Whether non-Jews are rewarded for keeping the seven מצוות בני נח, and the nations' claim against ישראל before הקדוש ברוך הוא
overview: This amud first finishes explaining what it means that הקדוש ברוך הוא 'released' the nations from the seven מצוות בני נח. The גמרא first says it means they get no reward for keeping them. רבי מאיר teaches that a גוי who learns תורה is like a כהן גדול, so the גמרא changes its answer: they get a smaller reward, like someone who is not commanded and does it anyway, as רבי חנינא teaches. Then the גמרא goes back to the story of the future judgment. The nations ask where ישראל actually kept the תורה. They reject God and heaven and earth as witnesses, until God brings witnesses from among the nations themselves. The nations then ask for the תורה again, and God gives them the easy מצוה of סוכה, even though this world is the only time for doing מצוות. They kick their סוכות away when the sun blazes, and the גמרא begins to explain on the next amud why that heat is not unfair.

steps.title: The release means no reward
steps.stepSummary: The 'release' of the nations from their מצוות means that even if they keep them, they get no reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to teach that even though they keep the מצוות, they get no reward for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining what it means that הקדוש ברוך הוא 'released' the nations. It says this does not mean the מצוות are cancelled. It means they get no reward for keeping them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier problem was that a sinner should not gain by being released from his duties. This answer avoids that problem. The nations are not freed from the מצוות. They simply lose the reward for keeping them.

keyTerms.meaning: to say / to teach (introduces what a source comes to teach)

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַיְּימִין אוֹתָן
phrases.english: To say that even though they fulfill them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the seven מצוות בני נח, which the גמרא was just talking about.

phrases.english: they do not receive reward for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר, שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּקַיְּימִין אוֹתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer given before this section to the question 'should a sinner gain?'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of 'release' as loss of reward, not loss of obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Released' means the nations no longer have to keep the מצוות, so sinners would gain.
steps.terutzMaskana: They still have the מצוות but receive no reward for keeping them.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי מאיר: a non-Jew learning Torah is like a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: a גוי who learns תורה is like a כהן גדול, which shows that non-Jews are rewarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they don't get reward? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי מאיר used to say: How do we know that even a non-Jew who learns תורה is like a כהן גדול? The פסוק says, 'which a person shall do and live by them.' It does not say 'כהנים, לוים and ישראלים', but 'a person'. So you learn that even a non-Jew who learns תורה is like a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last step. רבי מאיר gives a non-Jew who learns תורה a very high level, so how can we say non-Jews get no reward?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר learns from the word 'האדם' in the פסוק that the promise of 'life' is not only for Jews. If a גוי can reach the level of a כהן גדול through his תורה learning, he clearly gets reward. This goes directly against 'they receive no reward.'

keyTerms.meaning: the person (a general word for any human)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the high value of a non-Jew's תורה learning in the areas that apply to him.

phrases.english: And they don't? But isn't it taught:
Rabbi Meir would say:
From where do we know that even a non-Jew who engages in Torah
is like a High Priest?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר יַעֲשֶׂה אֹתָם הָאָדָם וָחַי בָּהֶם״,
phrases.english: The verse says: 'which a person shall do and live by them,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:5

phrases.english: it does not say 'Kohanim, Levites and Israelites,'
but rather 'the person,'

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָמַדְתָּ שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: so you have learned that even a non-Jew who engages in Torah
is like a High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 1 that the nations get no reward.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that non-Jews receive no reward for keeping their מצוות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר gives a non-Jew who learns תורה the level of a כהן גדול, which proves that non-Jews are rewarded.

steps.title: They get a smaller reward, like one not commanded
steps.stepSummary: Non-Jews do get reward, but only the lesser reward of someone who is not commanded and does it anyway, as רבי חנינא teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to tell you that they don't get reward like someone who is commanded and does it, but like someone who is not commanded and does it. As רבי חנינא said: one who is commanded and does is greater than one who is not commanded and does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes its answer from step 1. The nations do get reward, but a smaller kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'released' means the nations are now treated as if they were not commanded. So when they keep the מצוות, they get the lower reward of a volunteer. This fits with רבי מאיר, and רבי חנינא's rule shows that the commanded person's reward is greater.

keyTerms.meaning: one who is commanded and does the מצוה
one who is not commanded but does it anyway

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא: גדול המצווה ועושה יותר ממי שאינו מצווה ועושה. Doing a מצוה because you are commanded is worth more than doing it as a volunteer.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 1 is not being kept as it was. The גמרא now changes 'no reward' to 'less reward', the reward of someone not commanded.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי חנינא's rule is a basic idea about the value of being commanded, and it is quoted in many places.

phrases.english: Rather, it comes to tell you
that they do not receive reward for them
like one who is commanded and does,
but rather like one who is not commanded and does,
as Rabbi Chanina said:
Greater is one who is commanded and does
than one who is not commanded and does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2 by changing the answer of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Non-Jews get no reward at all for their מצוות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Non-Jews get the smaller reward of one who is not commanded and does, which still fits רבי מאיר.

steps.title: The nations ask: Where did ישראל keep the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the story of the future judgment. The nations ask הקדוש ברוך הוא where ישראל, who accepted the תורה, actually kept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the nations say before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the World, ישראל who accepted the תורה, where did they keep it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side discussion about reward and goes back to the conversation between הקדוש ברוך הוא and the nations. This line sets up the nations' next argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The nations' earlier claims were rejected because they did not keep even their seven מצוות. Now they change their approach and question ישראל instead. They say that accepting the תורה is not enough, and ask where ישראל actually kept it.

keyTerms.meaning: the Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: Rather, this is what the nations say
phrases.notes: 'Rather' brings us back to the story of the nations standing before הקדוש ברוך הוא in the future, which was left off earlier.

phrases.english: before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
Israel, who accepted it, where did they fulfill it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כָּךְ אוֹמְרִים הַגּוֹיִם לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about reward and goes back to the main story of the nations' claims.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nations argue that ישראל accepted the תורה but did not actually keep it.
steps.kashyaTarget: ישראל's claim to merit for having accepted the תורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Accepting the תורה is not enough; the nations demand proof that ישראל actually kept it.

steps.title: God offers to testify for ישראל Himself
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא answers the nations: He Himself will testify that ישראל kept the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא says to them: I testify about them that they kept the entire תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The nations asked where ישראל actually kept the תורה. הקדוש ברוך הוא answers that He Himself is the witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the first answer in a back-and-forth about witnesses. The story is built like a court case: one side brings a witness and the other side tries to disqualify him.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, says to them:
I testify about them
that they kept the entire Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אֲנִי מֵעִיד בָּהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the nations' question from step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where did ישראל keep the תורה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself testifies that they kept all of it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a witness to prove ישראל kept the תורה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no proof that ישראל actually kept the תורה they accepted.
steps.terutzMaskana: הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself testifies that ישראל kept the entire תורה.

steps.title: A father cannot testify for his son
steps.stepSummary: The nations object that God is ישראל's Father, and a father cannot testify about his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say before Him: Master of the Universe, can a father testify about his son? As it is written: 'My son, My firstborn, Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The nations try to disqualify God as a witness. They argue that He is a relative of ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a בית דין, a relative is not allowed to testify, and a father is a relative of his son. The פסוק calls ישראל God's son, so the nations say He is a disqualified witness.

keyTerms.meaning: is there at all? (a challenging question)

phrases.english: They say before Him: Master of the Universe,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ אָב שֶׁמֵּעִיד עַל בְּנוֹ?
phrases.english: is there a father who testifies about his son?
As it is written: "My son, My firstborn, Israel."
phrases.notes: שמות 4:22

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ אָב שֶׁמֵּעִיד עַל בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the witness offered in step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A relative is a disqualified witness. God is called ישראל's Father, so He cannot testify for them.

steps.title: Heaven and earth will testify
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא offers new witnesses: heaven and earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא says to them: Heaven and earth will testify about them that they kept the entire תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: God does not argue with the objection. He brings different witnesses instead: heaven and earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heaven and earth are not relatives of ישראל, so the father-son problem does not apply. God simply swaps in witnesses who avoid the nations' objection.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, says to them:
Heaven and earth will testify about them
that they kept the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by replacing the disqualified witness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: God Himself would be the witness.
steps.terutzMaskana: Heaven and earth, who are not relatives, will be the witnesses.

steps.title: Heaven and earth have a personal stake
steps.stepSummary: The nations object that heaven and earth gain from ישראל keeping the תורה, so their testimony is not trustworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say before Him: Master of the Universe, heaven and earth have a personal stake in their testimony, as it is said: 'If not for My covenant day and night, I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The nations try to disqualify heaven and earth too. They say these witnesses have something to gain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness who gains from the outcome (נוגע בעדותו) cannot testify. The פסוק says heaven and earth exist only because of God's covenant, so their own existence depends on ישראל and the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: they have a personal stake in their testimony

steps.confusionAlert: The nations are not saying heaven and earth would lie. They are using the court rule that someone who gains from his testimony is not accepted as a witness at all.

phrases.english: They say before Him: Master of the Universe,
heaven and earth have a personal stake in their testimony,
as it is said: "If not for My covenant day and night,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 33:25. The next steps show that "My covenant" here means the תורה.

phrases.english: I would not have set the laws of heaven and earth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new witnesses offered in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The testimony of heaven and earth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Their existence depends on the covenant of the תורה, so they gain if ישראל kept it. Such interested witnesses are not accepted.

steps.title: Creation depended on ישראל accepting the תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש teaches that God made Creation conditional on ישראל accepting the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: What is meant by what is written, 'And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day'? It teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא made a condition with the works of Creation and said: If ישראל accepts My תורה, good; and if not, I will return you to תוהו ובוהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that backs up the nations' claim. It shows that the whole world's existence hung on ישראל accepting the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Creation was given a condition: if ישראל did not accept the תורה, the world would go back to תוהו ובוהו. That is exactly why heaven and earth have a personal stake. Their survival depended on it.

keyTerms.meaning: emptiness and chaos (the state before Creation)

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון בן לקיש said:
phrases.notes: Some versions say דְּאָמַר ("as he said"). The better wording is וְאָמַר ("and he said").

phrases.english: What is meant by what is written:
"And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 1:31

phrases.english: It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made a condition
with the works of Creation, and said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקַבְּלִין אֶת תּוֹרָתִי מוּטָב,
phrases.english: If Israel accepts My Torah, good;
and if not —
I will return you to emptiness and chaos.
phrases.notes: "You" means the works of Creation themselves. God is speaking to the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 8 that heaven and earth have a stake.
steps.raayaObject: Heaven and earth are interested witnesses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון בן לקיש's reading of בראשית 1:31: Creation was conditional on ישראל accepting the תורה.

steps.title: The earth was afraid and then calm
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה's reading of a פסוק in תהלים shows that the earth feared until ישראל accepted the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what חזקיה said: What is meant by what is written, 'From heaven You made judgment heard; the earth feared and was calm'? If it feared, why was it calm, and if it was calm, why did it fear? Rather, at first it feared, and in the end it was calm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another source that fits the same idea. The earth was scared at מתן תורה because its existence was on the line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה points out that the פסוק seems to contradict itself, since fear and calm do not go together. He answers that they happened at two different times. The earth feared before ישראל accepted the תורה and calmed down after they did. This confirms that the earth had a personal stake.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is the same as
it was calm, it was quiet
at first ... and in the end

phrases.english: And this is what חזקיה said:
What is meant by what is written:
"From heaven You made judgment heard;
the earth feared and was calm"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 76:9

phrases.english: If it feared, why was it calm,
and if it was calm, why did it fear?
Rather, at first it feared,
and in the end it was calm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source matching רבי שמעון בן לקיש's idea from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The earth's fate depended on ישראל accepting the תורה, so it has a stake.
steps.raayaSupportSource: חזקיה's resolution of תהלים 76:9: first it feared, then it was calm.

steps.title: Witnesses from among the nations themselves
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא brings witnesses the nations cannot reject: their own people, who were enemies of the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא says to them: Let witnesses come from among you and testify about ישראל that they kept the entire תורה. Let נמרוד come and testify about אברהם that he did not worship עבודה זרה. Let לבן come and testify about יעקב that he is not suspected of robbery. Let אשת פוטיפרע come and testify about יוסף that he is not suspected of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: God answers the last objection by bringing witnesses from among the nations themselves. Each one opposed a righteous Jewish figure (אברהם, יעקב, יוסף), yet must admit that figure's righteousness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These witnesses are not relatives and gain nothing. In fact they were opponents, so the nations cannot reject them. נמרוד saw that אברהם would not serve עבודה זרה, לבן found nothing stolen by יעקב, and אשת פוטיפרע knows יוסף refused her.

keyTerms.meaning: the wife of Potiphar, who tried to seduce יוסף

steps.whatToRemember: Every witness for ישראל gets rejected: God is a 'relative' and heaven and earth have a stake. In the end the nations' own people prove the righteousness of ישראל's great figures. Their own witnesses defeat their claim.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, says to them:
From among you let them come and testify
about them, about Israel,
that they kept the entire Torah.
Let Nimrod come and testify about Abraham
that he did not worship idols;
let Laban come and testify about Jacob
that he is not suspected of robbery;
phrases.notes: See בראשית 31:36–42.

phrases.english: let Potiphar's wife come and testify about Joseph
that he is not suspected of the sin.
phrases.notes: "The sin" means sinning with a married woman. See בראשית 39:7–12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of steps 8–10 by bringing witnesses with no stake.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the witnesses with ones the other side cannot reject
steps.terutzMaskana: The nations' own people, who were hostile to the אבות, testify to their righteousness.

steps.title: More witnesses from the nations testify for Israel
steps.stepSummary: The list continues: נבוכדנצר, דריוש, and the friends of איוב will testify that ישראל were faithful, as the פסוק says 'let them bring their witnesses.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Let נבוכדנצר come and testify that חנניה, מישאל and עזריה did not bow to the idol. Let דריוש come and testify that דניאל did not stop praying. Let בלדד, צופר, אליפז and אליהו come and testify that ישראל kept the whole תורה. As the פסוק says: 'Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list of witnesses from step 11. These are people from the nations themselves who saw Jews stay loyal to God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These witnesses cannot be dismissed the way heaven and earth were in step 8. They gain nothing from ישראל keeping the תורה, and some were even the ones who tried to force them to sin. The פסוק from ישעיהו supports the idea that the nations' own witnesses will prove ישראל right.

keyTerms.meaning: let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified

steps.whatToRemember: The final witnesses come from the nations themselves, so the nations have no way to reject them.

phrases.english: Let Nebuchadnezzar come and testify
about Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah
that they did not bow down to the idol.
phrases.notes: דניאל 3

phrases.english: Let Darius come and testify about Daniel
that he did not stop his prayer.
phrases.notes: דניאל 6

phrases.english: Let Bildad the Shuhite come,
and Zophar the Naamathite, and Eliphaz the Temanite,
phrases.notes: These are the friends of איוב from ספר איוב.

phrases.english: and Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite,
and let them testify about them, about Israel,
that they kept the entire Torah.
phrases.notes: Meaning: these people saw Jews keep the whole תורה.

phrases.english: As it is said: "Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 43:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of trustworthy witnesses begun in step 11 and ends with a supporting פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing rejected witnesses with witnesses who cannot be suspected
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses from the nations, who gain nothing from ישראל, testify to ישראל's faithfulness.

steps.title: The nations ask for the Torah again
steps.stepSummary: After losing the case, the nations ask God to give them the תורה over again so they can keep it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said before Him: Master of the World, give it to us again from the start, and we will do it.
steps.whatsHappening: The nations admit they lost and ask for a second chance. This sets up God's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the nations argued that they were not given a fair chance. Now they change approach and ask for the תורה again right now. The question is whether keeping מצוות is still possible at this point.

phrases.english: They said before Him: Master of the World,
give it to us from the start, and we will do it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, תְּנֶהָ לָנוּ מֵרֹאשׁ וְנַעֲשֶׂנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the testimony defeats them, the nations ask for a second chance.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the nations receive the תורה now and keep it?

steps.title: God says it is too late, but offers the easy מצוה of סוכה
steps.stepSummary: God calls the nations fools: whoever prepared on ערב שבת eats on שבת, and whoever did not has nothing. Still, He offers them the easy מצוה of סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to them: Fools of the world! Whoever worked hard on ערב שבת will eat on שבת. Whoever did not work hard on ערב שבת, where will he get food on שבת? But even so, I have an easy מצוה called סוכה. Go and do it.
steps.whatsHappening: God answers with a משל: the time for doing מצוות has passed. Even so, He gives the nations one easy מצוה to try.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערב שבת is the time to prepare, and שבת is when you enjoy what you prepared. The nations' chance to do מצוות is over, so the plain answer is no. Then the story adds a twist: God still gives them סוכה as a test.
steps.confusionAlert: The משל seems to close the door completely, and then God offers a מצוה anyway. This tension is exactly what the גמרא will challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
Fools of the world!
One who worked hard on Shabbos eve
will eat on Shabbos.
One who did not work hard on Shabbos eve,
from where will he eat on Shabbos?
But even so,
I have an easy מצוה,
and its name is sukkah.
Go and do it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: שׁוֹטִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the nations' request: it is too late, but they are offered סוכה anyway.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The time to prepare has passed, yet God offers the nations the easy מצוה of סוכה.

steps.title: Challenge: מצוות can only be done in this world
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how God could offer a מצוה at that time, since רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that 'today', this world, is for doing מצוות, and not 'tomorrow'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say that? But רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What does the פסוק mean, 'which I command you today'? Today is for doing them, not tomorrow. Today is for doing them, and today is not for receiving reward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now steps out of the story and challenges it. A מצוה offered at the final judgment seems to contradict a known teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'today' in the פסוק as this world, the only time for doing מצוות. The future is for reward, not for new מצוות. So how could God offer the nations סוכה after this world has ended?
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching is a famous basic idea: this world is the time for doing, and the next world is the time for reward.

phrases.english: And can you really say so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
What is meant by what is written: "which I command you today"?
phrases.notes: דברים 7:11

phrases.english: Today is for doing them,
phrases.notes: "Today" means this world, and "tomorrow" means the world to come.

phrases.english: and tomorrow is not for doing them.
Today is for doing them,
and today is not for receiving reward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges God's offer of סוכה in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that God offers the nations a מצוה at the final judgment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that מצוות can be done only in this world, so no מצוה can be offered afterward.

steps.title: God does not deal unfairly with His creations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that God offers סוכה anyway because He does not deal harshly or unfairly with His creations. He wants them to see they had a fair chance.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because הקדוש ברוך הוא does not deal unfairly with His creations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The offer of סוכה is not a real return to the time for doing מצוות; God makes it so the nations cannot complain they were treated unfairly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule stays in place. The סוכה offer is a special exception, given so that the nations' failure will be clear and God's judgment will be seen as fair.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not
deal unfairly with His creations.
phrases.notes: בִּטְרוּנְיָא means making harsh, one-sided demands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שֶׁאֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the purpose of the offer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סוכה offer means מצוות can still be done after this world.
steps.terutzMaskana: The offer is a one-time chance so that God's judgment is clearly fair, not a real return to the time of doing.

steps.title: Why is סוכה called an easy מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why God called סוכה an 'easy מצוה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does He call it an 'easy מצוה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the wording in step 14. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building a סוכה takes effort, so calling it 'easy' needs an explanation. The גמרא wants to know in what way it is easy.

phrases.english: And why does He call it an "easy מצוה"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to God's words in step 14 to explain one phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what sense is סוכה an 'easy' מצוה?

steps.title: סוכה is easy because it costs no money
steps.stepSummary: סוכה is called easy because doing it involves no loss of money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it involves no loss of money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: סוכה is 'easy' because it does not cost money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Easy' here does not mean it takes no effort. It means the person loses no money doing it, so the nations have no excuse not to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: loss of money (literally, 'a lack in the pocket')

phrases.english: Because it involves no loss of money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סוכה is 'easy' because it costs no money.

steps.title: The nations build סוכות but kick them away in the heat
steps.stepSummary: Each nation builds a סוכה on its roof. God makes the sun burn as in the season of תמוז, and each one kicks his סוכה and leaves, fulfilling the פסוק 'Let us break their bands.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, every one of them takes materials and builds a סוכה on his roof. Then הקדוש ברוך הוא makes the sun blaze like the summer heat of תמוז. Each one kicks his סוכה and walks out. As the פסוק says: 'Let us break their bands and cast away their cords from us.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The nations accept the easy מצוה of סוכה, but as soon as it becomes uncomfortable, they kick it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test shows what the nations are really like. They do not just leave the סוכה, which would be understandable in great heat. They kick it, showing contempt for the מצוה. The פסוק from תהלים describes exactly this: throwing off God's 'bands' and 'cords.'

keyTerms.meaning: makes (the sun) blaze or burn hot
the season of תמוז, the hottest part of summer

steps.confusionAlert: Leaving the סוכה is not the main failure, since great discomfort can excuse a person from sitting in it. The failure is that they kick the סוכה on the way out, which shows contempt for the מצוה.

phrases.english: Immediately, each and every one takes
and goes and makes a סוכה on top of his roof,
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, makes blaze upon them
the sun, as in the season of תמוז,
phrases.notes: תמוז is the height of summer, so the heat is fierce.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מְבַעֵט בְּסוּכָּתוֹ וְיוֹצֵא,
phrases.english: and each and every one kicks his סוכה and leaves,
as it is said:
"Let us break their bands
and cast away their cords from us."
phrases.notes: תהלים 2:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about why סוכה is called easy, the גמרא returns to the story and tells what the nations do with the מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The nations build סוכות, but when God brings intense heat, they kick their סוכות and leave, rejecting the מצוה.

steps.title: Isn't heating the sun harsh treatment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how God could make the sun blaze, when we said He does not deal harshly with His creations.
steps.simpleTranslation: He makes the sun blaze? But you said that הקדוש ברוך הוא does not deal harshly with His creations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. Heating the sun looks like setting the nations up to fail, and that seems to contradict what was said earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said God offers סוכה because He does not deal with His creations in a harsh or unfair way. Making the test unbearable with extreme heat seems to be exactly that kind of unfair treatment. The two parts of the story now seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't you say? (pointing to an earlier statement that seems to conflict)

phrases.english: He makes the sun blaze?
But didn't you say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not come with harshness
toward His creations!
phrases.notes: This is the same rule the גמרא used a moment ago to explain why God offers them סוכה at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the detail of the heat in step 19, using the principle stated in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The detail that God makes the sun blaze over the nations' סוכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If God never deals harshly with His creations, He should not make the test unbearable by heating the sun.

steps.title: The Jewish people also face such times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer that the heat is not unfair, because the Jewish people also sometimes face such conditions. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because for the Jewish people as well, there are times...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer. It compares the nations to the Jewish people, who also sometimes face this kind of situation. The rest of the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer moves the heat from 'unfair treatment' to 'normal conditions that everyone faces.' If the Jewish people also live through such heat, then the nations are not being singled out. The full answer is completed on the next amud.

phrases.english: Because for the Jewish people as well, there are times

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison: the condition is shared by the Jewish people, so it is not harsh treatment aimed at the nations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the heat was a special hardship designed to make the nations fail.
steps.terutzMaskana: The heat is something the Jewish people also face at times, so it is a fair test and not unfair treatment (the answer continues on the next amud).
